prompt.en: A project folder has one tab for the local process and one tab for CPC-2-0-03. What is the best two-step use of those tabs?

text.en: Check the local-process tab for municipal instructions, check the CPC tab as ISED antenna-siting material, then choose the process path from those sources
Use the CPC tab only after the municipality has rejected every local exclusion
Merge both tabs into one rule that requires a matching exclusion in both sources every time
File CPC-2-0-03 as a Health Canada RF exposure document instead of an antenna-siting procedure

explanation.en: The lesson separates municipal process material from ISED antenna-siting material. CPC-2-0-03 belongs with antenna consultation, not with Health Canada RF exposure or EMCAB-2 complaint handling.

prompt.en: Which note about Safety Code 6 is NOT true?

text.en: It is the Health Canada exposure guideline named in this lesson
It deals with limits for people exposed to RF energy
It is the EMCAB-2 procedure for deciding interference complaints at affected premises
It is separate from the antenna-siting consultation path

explanation.en: Safety Code 6 is the RF exposure guideline. EMCAB-2 is the separate field-strength framework used for electromagnetic compatibility complaints.

prompt.en: A troubleshooting sheet says, 'If the affected device is in a home, use the associated-equipment category and do not read the device type.' What error should you spot?

text.en: Associated equipment is not a catch-all for every household device; identify the equipment category before applying the criterion
Associated equipment is never used for home-entertainment devices
Equipment category matters only for antenna-siting consultation
Once field strength is measured, the equipment category can always be ignored

explanation.en: EMCAB-2 uses equipment categories as part of choosing the applicable field-strength criterion; the lesson does not make associated equipment a universal household label.
